author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: processFindForm passes the raw, unclamped page argument to addPaginationModel (line 121: `return addPaginationModel(page, model, ownersResults)`), so the currentPage model attribute is set to 0 or a negative number when ?page=0 or ?page=-5 is requested. The clamping introduced in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName corrects the repository query (data is fetched from page 1) but the view receives a stale currentPage value. Any pagination link or display that reads currentPage from the model will show the wrong page number, and a 'previous page' link computed as currentPage-1 will produce -1. The fix is incomplete: either clamp page to effectivePage at the processFindForm call site before passing it to both helpers, or propagate the effective value out of findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and use it consistently.

processFindFormWithZeroPageReturnsFirstPage and processFindFormWithNegativePageReturnsFirstPage assert only the view name; neither verifies model().attribute("currentPage", 1). The method names promise that the first page is returned, but the assertions do not back that claim and would pass even when currentPage is set to 0 or -5 in the model. Add .andExpect(model().attribute("currentPage", 1)) to both tests so they pin the behavior the names describe and would catch the incomplete fix identified above.
findings.fix: Add `.andExpect(model().attribute("currentPage", 1))` to the perform chain in both processFindFormWithZeroPageReturnsFirstPage and processFindFormWithNegativePageReturnsFirstPage.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The two new tests assert HTTP 200 and the view name but not that the model presents page 1 to the user. The stated contract is that the listing renders as the first page, not merely that no exception is thrown. The production method addPaginationModel receives the raw page parameter and writes model.addAttribute("currentPage", page), so with page=0 the model carries currentPage=0 and with page=-5 it carries currentPage=-5. The template would display 'Page 0 of N' — the very symptom the fix should eliminate — yet the tests pass. Add model().attribute("currentPage", is(1)) to both assertions (or to the merged parameterized test). Also add a Pageable argument capture to verify the repository is called with PageRequest.of(0, pageSize), confirming the clamping is applied.

The local variable is named 'tasks' in both new tests. The name has no relation to the domain object (a Page<Owner>). Use a role-describing name such as 'multipleOwnersPage' to satisfy the Three-Tier Data Naming convention (Tier 3 eliminated). This is the same copy-paste name visible in processFindFormSuccess at line 146 — both pre-existing and new tests carry the defect; the brief requires moving construction at the test-touch point.
findings.fix: Rename local variable 'tasks' to 'multipleOwnersPage' (or equivalent role name) in both new tests.

findings.description: Two near-identical tests covering sub-1 page values (0 and -5) should be a single @ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource. The brief (testing-principles.md § Agent Decision Checklist item on parameterized tests) requires this for repetitive cases. Extract a single method such as theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsBelowOne with a @CsvSource carrying both values.

Test method names use the implementation-naming style ('processFindFormWith...') rather than the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school required since 2026-07-31 (testing-principles.md § Test Naming). The brief says a slice touching a test renames only that test. Rename to describe the behavior, e.g. theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsZero and theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsNegative (or collapse into one parameterized test per the prior finding).
findings.fix: Rename to the{Subject}Should{Outcome} form per the brief's BDD school.

findings.description: No blank line separates the Arrange phase (PageImpl construction + stub setup) from the Act/Assert chain. The brief (testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure) requires phases to be separated by blank lines alone.
findings.fix: Add a blank line between the when(...).thenReturn(...) line and the mockMvc.perform(...) line in both tests.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Relocated single-point clamp is now the sole source of the page value: effectivePage = Math.max(page, 1) is computed once at the processFindForm entry (line 99) and passed to BOTH consumers - findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (line 111) and addPaginationModel (line 125). The raw page variable is referenced nowhere else, so no unclamped page reaches the query path or the view model.

No underflow: PageRequest.of(effectivePage - 1, 5) at line 139 has effectivePage >= 1, so the zero-based index is always >= 0; Integer.MIN_VALUE clamps to 1 before the -1, so no negative PageRequest index can be constructed.

No integer-overflow / negative-offset exposure: large page values keep PageRequest.getOffset() in long arithmetic ((long)index*size); the query returns an empty page which routes to the notFound branch, never a negative SQL offset.
page binds to a primitive int via @RequestParam, so non-numeric input fails at Spring type binding (400) rather than crossing the pagination trust boundary; no injection vector.
lastName flows through the parameterized Spring Data derived query findByLastNameStartingWith (no SQLi) and currentPage renders as an int through auto-escaped Thymeleaf (no XSS).

Parameterized MockMvc test (page=0, -5) pins currentPage == 1 and verifies the repository is called with PageRequest.of(0, 5), confirming the clamp reaches both the view and the query consistently after relocation.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The literal 5 in PageRequest.of(0, 5) is a Tier 3 mystery value (testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming Convention). The production method findPaginatedForOwnersLastName stores the page size as a local variable `int pageSize = 5` — not a named, accessible constant — leaving the test and production coupled only by an unnamed number. Add a test-local named variable `int expectedPageSize = 5` before the verify call (or extract a package-private constant from OwnerController and reference it). The zero in PageRequest.of(0, ...) is self-documenting as the zero-based index of the first page and does not need a name.
findings.fix: Add `int expectedPageSize = 5;` before the verify line and change the argument to `eq(PageRequest.of(0, expectedPageSize))`. Alternatively, extract `static final int PAGE_SIZE = 5` in OwnerController (package-private) and reference it from the test.

approved_aspects: Finding 1 resolved: model().attribute("currentPage", 1) is now asserted at line 162, pinning the clamped page value in the view model; this assertion would fail on unfixed production code because addPaginationModel would receive the raw page value and set currentPage to 0 or -5.
Finding 2 resolved: local variable renamed from tasks to multipleOwnersPage at line 157, satisfying the three-tier naming convention for the Arrange phase.
Finding 3 resolved: two near-identical tests merged into a single @ParameterizedTest @CsvSource({"0","-5"}) void theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsBelowOne(int page) at lines 154-166.
Finding 4 resolved: method name follows the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school required since 2026-07-31.
Finding 5 resolved: blank line between Arrange (lines 157-158) and Act/Assert (lines 160-163), and another blank line before the verify (line 165), satisfying the four-phase separation rule.

Regression-guard soundness confirmed: without Math.max(page,1) the raw page=0 flows into PageRequest.of(-1,5) which throws IllegalArgumentException, producing a 500 that fails status().isOk(); the model().attribute("currentPage",1) then catches any partial fix where the query is clamped but addPaginationModel still receives the raw value. Both assertions are genuine regression guards.

verify call correctly confirms the repository receives PageRequest.of(0,5) — zero-based first-page index with page size 5 — and uses Mockito ArgumentMatchers.eq for exact Pageable matching rather than any(Pageable.class).
MockMvc is the sanctioned web-layer test harness; OwnerRepository mock is tolerated existing-suite usage per the mocking policy.
@ParameterizedTest with @CsvSource covers both boundary values (0 and -5) in one method, eliminating duplication.
